text:
olga: Heads up — we're seeing a sharp IOPS variance and some read retries on local SSDs in us-west2 during the 02:30 UTC GPU-provisioning window. GPU attach failures climbed from ~0.2% to ~3% across the pool. Noticed higher scrub activity on ephemeral drives.

infra-bot: [alert] nvme_io_variance detected (us-west2). metric: nvme.read_retries spike -> threshold exceeded. incident created #INC-1234.

sam: Can you paste a short dmesg / nvme-cli output from one of affected nodes?

olga: quick snippets from host gnode-uw2-31 (redacted):
```
[Feb 18 02:30:12] nvme0: I/O 0x7f failed, status: 0x2, retries=3
[Feb 18 02:30:13] nvme0n1: read timeout, requeued
[Feb 18 02:30:14] nvme0: admin queue stalled, controller reset
```

olga: and the janitor/cleaner logs around that time:
```
2026-02-18T02:29:50 cleaner[pid=4123] starting deep-scrub /scratch/ephemeral --concurrency=4
2026-02-18T02:30:10 cleaner[pid=4123] read-errors=12, avg-iops=24k
2026-02-18T02:30:11 gpu-provisioner attach failed node=gnode-uw2-31 reason=io-timeout
```

maya: sounds like background scrub concurrency is contending with attach IO. Short-term mitigations: throttle the cleaner (concurrency -> 1) or pause deep-scrubs in us-west2 for the next 30m, and enable attach fallback to different AZ if attach latency > X ms.

ton y: Cost tradeoff note: switching new attaches to network-backed volumes reduces local attach failures but adds ~10–15% per-GPU monthly cost and latency bump. For short-term outage it's OK; long-term we should fix cleaner scheduling.

sam: Commands if someone wants to run quick mitigation on the canary node: 
```bash
ssh gnode-uw2-31 sudo systemctl stop ephemeral-cleaner.service || sudo pkill -f ephemeral-cleaner
# reduce concurrency in SSM param store for cleaner service:
aws ssm put-parameter --name "/infra/cleaner/concurrency" --value "1" --type String --overwrite --region us-west-2
```

sam: Also ran nvme-cli checks on the canary: `sudo nvme smart-log /dev/nvme0` returned 8 read retry increments and increased temperature by ~6C vs baseline.

olga: I ran the concurrency flip in the canary pool (set param -> 1) at 02:36 UTC and paused deep-scrubs for 30m. Attach failures dropped to ~0.6% within 8 minutes. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: #INC-1234 updated: mitigation applied (cleaner concurrency=1) — monitoring.

maya: For next steps: add a cleaner-slo that avoids heavy scrubs during the 02:00-03:00 provisioning window, add health-check to detect nvme read-retries and temporarily reduce cleaner activity, and schedule a firmware/SMART audit on top offenders.

ton y: I'll run an ROI calc for moving some high-density pools to remote block store vs reworking cleaner scheduling. Short-term we keep the reduced concurrency and monitor cost/attach success.

olga: Filed follow-up ticket in infra board: INFRA-502 (investigate cleaner-scheduling + scrub backoff on nvme read retries). Will post a short blameless postmortem if the rate stays up. Thanks all for quick triage.

sam: Nice work. I'll keep an eye and push a small playbook entry for on-call: how to throttle cleaner and validate attach success.

tony: :rocket:

infra-bot: Monitoring note: attach_success_rate (us-west2) back to baseline? 0.8% -> continuing to observe for 60m."
